description:
## Outcome

The OTP application contains an optional daemon supervision boundary. Normal application start does not start the daemon.

## Why now

The package spike needs a supervised foreground process, but the application now has no OTP application module or daemon boundary.

## Work

1. Add `Jido.Cli.Application` and the named `Jido.Cli.Daemon`, `Supervisor`, `Server`, `Client`, and `Protocol` module boundaries from `RELEASE_PLAN.md`.
2. Keep the normal application tree small and start daemon children only through an explicit daemon start API.
3. Define start, already-started, stop, and child-start failure results.
4. Let the daemon boundary start without provider credentials.
5. Make child specifications and dependencies suitable for a foreground service manager.
6. Add deterministic child-start, start-race, partial-start cleanup, and clean-stop tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Starting `:jido_cli` does not start a daemon listener or daemon worker.
- [ ] The explicit daemon start API returns one supervised tree.
- [ ] Concurrent starts have one owner and a stable loser result.
- [ ] Missing provider credentials do not prevent the daemon tree from starting.
- [ ] A child-start failure leaves no partial daemon tree.
- [ ] The boundary has no backgrounding or OS-service logic.

## Tests

Add application and daemon supervisor tests with injected child modules. Run `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not route CLI commands, implement transport, install a service, or make local CLI modes use the daemon in this task.
title: Add the optional daemon application supervision boundary
